vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.21

The 'memclaw' skill bundle provides a sophisticated tiered memory management system (L0/L1/L2) for OpenClaw agents, using a custom 'cortex://' URI scheme. The documentation (SKILL.md, tools.md) describes tools for semantic search, hierarchical browsing, and session-based memory storage, all of which are consistent with the stated purpose of enhancing AI memory efficiency. Security documentation (security.md) explicitly states that data is stored locally and no external exfiltration occurs, and no malicious patterns, obfuscation, or harmful prompt injections were identified in the instructions.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions and tools are coherent for a local memory plugin, but this package is instruction-only and directs you to install external plugin code from an unknown source (no homepage or bundled install), which raises supply-chain and provenance concerns.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a memory plugin) matches the operations described (search, browse, layered recall, migration). The declared requirements in this bundle (none) are consistent with an instruction-only wrapper that delegates runtime work to an external plugin. However, the skill tells the agent to install '@memclaw/memclaw' via the OpenClaw plugin manager — that external install is required for actual functionality but is not included in this package, so provenance matters.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read, list, and retrieve user memory (cortex:// URIs), migrate built-in memory, and call local services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service). Those actions are expected for a memory plugin, but they inherently grant access to potentially sensitive local data. The instructions do not attempt to read unrelated system paths or hidden credentials; they focus on OpenClaw memory and plugin config.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in this package; instead the instructions direct the user to run 'openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw' to obtain the actual plugin. The skill bundle provides no homepage or repository link and the registry owner is an opaque ID, so the actual code that would be installed is external and unreviewed here — this is a supply-chain/provenance risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: This skill requests no environment variables or credentials itself. It does require that the host's OpenClaw plugin settings be configured with an LLM/embedding provider (handled by OpenClaw), which is reasonable. Still, because the plugin operates over user memory, ensure that any provider API keys remain protected by OpenClaw and are not exposed by the installed plugin.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated privileges in the registry metadata (always:false). It does instruct changing OpenClaw config (disabling built-in memorySearch) to avoid conflicts, which is a local configuration change but not inherently privileged. Autonomous agent invocation (disable-model-invocation:false) is default and not by itself a concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This instruction-only skill describes a local memory system and will work only if you install the actual '@memclaw/memclaw' plugin it references. Before installing: verify the plugin's registry page or source repository and publisher reputation (no homepage is listed here), inspect the plugin code or release artifacts for network calls or data exfiltration, and consider testing in an isolated environment. Be aware that the plugin will access your OpenClaw memory (cortex:// URIs) and may require local services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service). Keep your LLM/embedding API keys managed by OpenClaw's secure settings and do not publicly share openclaw.json. If you cannot verify the plugin's origin or code, treat the external install as a supply-chain risk and avoid installing it on sensitive systems.
